startup.name: Sira
startup.one_liner: AI Native Rippling for Deskless Workers
startup.description: AI powered platform for time tracking, scheduling, payroll and HR for hourly teams. Agents call workers to fill open shifts, detect timesheet anomalies and streamline payroll. Four person team in San Francisco, B2B HR.

yc_acceptance.basis: Prior of about 1 percent (yc_acceptance.md, range 0.6 to 2 percent). Up for AI agents solving a concrete scheduling pain and a clear buyer; down because the description is a broad suite against Deputy, Homebase and Rippling, and payroll is a heavy regulatory build for four people. Net about 1.2 percent. The company is already in the Summer 2025 batch, shown for completeness.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because a full time, scheduling, payroll and HR suite for hourly workers is a large scope for four founders and the market has Homebase, Deputy and 7shifts. Partners would want a narrow wedge such as shift filling with paying customers before expanding to payroll.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: seed 49% / 59% / 65% (cond 59%, n=126). time_to_milestones.csv industry:B2B months_to_seed p25 3, median 7, p75 20; era:2022+ median 6, p75 14.2.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 16.3 months from 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17 and the target is an outside round above about $1M. About 75 percent of eventual seeds in the 2022+ timing table are in by month 16. 0.59 x 0.75 x 0.95 for excluding the YC deal is about 0.42. No lift for the AI agent framing per the winners test; these odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M, like Hammr's 2023 seed from Pioneer Fund for construction workforce software.
Institutional seed with early customers, near the 2022+ B2B median of $3.5M.
Larger seed if the shift filling agents show strong usage and revenue.
Upside if growth is fast enough for a lead from a top fund.

ladder.why_it_fails: Seed fails if the product looks like many existing scheduling tools with an AI label. Homebase claims 150,000 small businesses and native payroll, Deputy and 7shifts own scheduling, and earlier YC peers show the range: Zeal raised a $1.6M seed in 2020, Shift Messenger raised $1.5M in 2015 and went inactive, and Hammr raised a small seed. A four person team building payroll must also clear compliance work before it can sell.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: series_a cond 26% (n=74); months_to_series_a 2022+ median 28, p25 19.4.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 16.3 months total, before the 2022+ p25 of 19 months to Series A. Only a fast tail gets there, so 0.26 x about 0.3 is 0.08; this is more than 2x below the ever anchor because of timing.

bands.rationale: Smaller A for an HR and payroll startup with modest ARR.
Typical 2022+ A, median $15M, with payroll revenue growing.
Upside A for rapid expansion across hourly industries.

ladder.why_it_fails: Payroll and HR products need many customers to build revenue, and onboarding each employer is slow. Zeal took until after a 2020 seed to raise an A, and Instawork needed years. Without a segment where it dominates, investors see a feature set against established rivals.

bands.rationale: Modest Series B round with solid ARR and early expansion across several industries.
Typical Series B for HR software, near the 2022+ median of $40M.
Upside if the company becomes a leader for deskless workforce management.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B is a stage few seed companies reach. By then the company would compete with Rippling and Paychex, which acquired Paycor in April 2025, and Deputy. Payroll margins are modest, and winning needs distribution advantages that a young startup lacks, and investors would look for net revenue retention above 100 percent.

bands.rationale: Typical Series C round, with the 2022+ table median at $74M and post money near $1.2B.
Strong growth case with payroll scale and a high valuation near the top of the range.
Flat or down round if payroll growth slows.

ladder.why_it_fails: Few payroll startups reach this stage. Late stage payroll competition favors consolidators with large bases such as Paychex and Rippling, and a stall in customer growth would end the funding path, because late investors want rising net retention, clean payroll margins and a defensible position against the largest payroll platforms.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Hourly workforce software is crowded and consolidating, and payroll is slow to build. Most paths end in a stall or acquisition by a larger payroll or scheduling vendor, as with Shift Messenger which went inactive after a seed. A large exit would need Sira to out-execute Homebase and Deputy.

killers.risk: Established scheduling and payroll vendors dominate
killers.evidence: Homebase claims 150,000 businesses with native payroll and Deputy and 7shifts own scheduling.
killers.mitigation: Win one vertical, such as restaurants or healthcare staffing, with AI shift filling.

killers.risk: Payroll compliance and trust burden for a four person team
killers.evidence: Payroll requires tax filing and state registrations in many states, which slows launch and adds liability.
killers.mitigation: Partner with a payroll engine and sell scheduling first.

killers.risk: Agent calling workers fails on reliability or regulation
killers.evidence: Automated calls to workers face telecom rules and reliability issues.
killers.mitigation: Start with text messages and opt in flows.

competition_now.name: Homebase
competition_now.what: Scheduling, time tracking and native payroll for SMBs
competition_now.traction: Claims 150,000 businesses and 1.2 billion hours logged in a year

competition_now.name: Deputy
competition_now.what: Scheduling with AI forecasting, payroll via Paycor partnership
competition_now.traction: Plans at $30 to $54 per month in a vendor comparison

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling and time tracking are straightforward; payroll tax and compliance plus reliable voice or text agents are harder, and four engineers can ship scheduling in 3 months but payroll takes longer.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents with large bases can add AI shift filling in months and already own payroll distribution, so the agent feature alone is a thin defense against copying.

evidence.claim: Hourly workforce tools are a paid category with vendors claiming 150,000 customers and per month pricing.
Paychex completed its Paycor acquisition on April 14, 2025, showing consolidation and demand in payroll.

actions: Sign five employers on shift filling
Track fill rate against manual calling
Add payroll via a partner for existing customers
roadmap.proof: $40K MRR with payroll attach above 30 percent

pros.point: Large hourly workforce category that pays
pros.evidence: Competitors report 150,000 customers and monthly plans.

pros.point: Concrete agent use case with measurable value
pros.evidence: Filling open shifts by calling workers has a clear before and after metric.

brand.name: Sira
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Sira" --era 2022+: invented or proper, 4 chars
brand.rationale: Short coined names such as Rippling-era HR brands work when the product wins; Sira is short and friendly but meaningless, which neither helps nor hurts much.

narrative.headline: A broad AI native suite for hourly workers against entrenched scheduling and payroll vendors.
narrative.general_summary: Sira offers AI agents plus time, scheduling, payroll and HR for hourly teams. The forecast window is 16.3 months from 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17. We estimate 0.42 for an outside round above about $1M closing inside the window, from the 2022 to 2025 B2B anchor of 0.59 scaled for timing, with no AI hype lift. Analogs include Zeal and Instawork that raised, and Shift Messenger that went inactive. These odds do not rank this company against others. Reaching a round later is common for companies with paying customers.

assumptions: Only the input file and market searches were used.
Seed means an outside round above about $1M.
